tagline: Twelve winding miles to the northwest corner of the lower 48.
intro: SR 112 comes west along the Strait of Juan de Fuca, past Sekiu and over the Hoko River, with viewpoints looking across the water to Vancouver Island. At the mouth of the Sail River it enters the Makah Reservation, and from there it is about 12 miles of winding road through Neah Bay to the trailhead for Cape Flattery.
It was the first tribal road given scenic status, crossing the home of the Makah, who have lived here for thousands of years. It is also the only road that goes to the cape.

moments.title: Makah Museum, Neah Bay
moments.text: The museum keeps the canoes, basketry and whaling gear of a Makah village at Ozette that a mudslide buried, with a replica longhouse among them.

moments.title: Cape Flattery
moments.text: James Cook named the point in 1778 for an opening that flattered him with hopes of a harbour, and a trail, mostly boardwalk, now goes out through the forest to it.

moments.title: Tatoosh Island
moments.text: Seen from the cape, the island has kept a lighthouse since 1857, though no one lives there now and landing takes the Makah tribe's written permission.

practical: A Makah Recreation Permit must be displayed in the vehicle for outdoor activities along the byway.
